NONE: C1 to accept, admit, or recognize something, or the truth or existence of something
C1 to tell someone, usually in a letter or email, that you have received something they sent you
（通過信函或電子郵件等）確認收悉

example: [ + -ing verb ] She acknowledged having been at fault.
她承認自己有過錯。
[ + that ] She acknowledged that she had been at fault.
她承認自己有過錯。
You must acknowledge the truth of her argument.
你必須承認她論點的真實性。
Historians generally acknowledge her as a genius in her field.
歷史學家公認她是該領域中的天才。
[ + obj + to infinitive ] She is usually acknowledged to be one of our best artists.
她通常被認為是我們這個時代最偉大的藝術家之一。
They refused to acknowledge (= to recognize officially) the new government.
他們拒絕承認新政府。
He didn't even acknowledge my presence (= show that he had seen me).
他見到我連個招呼都沒有打。
The government won't even acknowledge the existence of the problem.
政府甚至都不承認這個問題的存在。
Please acknowledge receipt of this letter.
收到此信，請覆函告知。

C or U: › [ C or U ] the fact of accepting that something is true or right
承認；認可…的屬實或存在
› something given to thank someone for what they have done
› a letter or email to say that something has been received
› a short text at the beginning or end of a book where the writer names people or other works that have helped in writing the book
（作者在卷首或卷末的）致謝，鳴謝，感謝

example: All I want is some acknowledgment that his behaviour is unreasonable.
我只要你們承認他的行為是無理取鬧就好。
We sent her a copy of the book in acknowledgment of her part in its creation.
我們寄給她一本書以感謝她為這本書的問世所做的貢獻。
I applied for four jobs, but I've only had one acknowledgment so far.
我申請了四份工作，可到現在只收到一封告知收悉的回信。
